claim: Tissue regeneration enhancer elements (TREEs) direct expression of target genes in injured and regenerating tissues.
source: Tissue regeneration enhancer elements (TREEs) direct expression of target genes in injured and regenerating tissues.
evidence: This is a foundational statement about TREEs that is supported by citations to prior work and experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: TREEs of zebrafish origin direct expression of transgenes in border zone regions after cardiac injury when packaged into recombinant adeno-associated viral (AAV) vectors and introduced into mice.
source: Additionally, TREEs of zebrafish origin were shown to direct expression of transgenes in border zone regions after cardiac injury when packaged into recombinant adeno-associated viral (AAV) vectors and introduced into mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by prior published work and is referenced in the abstract as established knowledge.

claim: Longitudinal tracking of expression directed by different TREEs revealed distinct amplitudes and durations of reporter gene expression in the injured heart.
source: Longitudinal tracking of expression directed by different TREEs revealed distinct amplitudes and durations of reporter gene expression in the injured heart.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from IVIS imaging experiments shown in the manuscript.

claim: The liver-de-targeted AAV capsid, AAV.cc84, can deliver TREEs either pre- or post-cardiac injury to negate off-target expression in the liver while maintaining transduction in the heart.
source: The liver-de-targeted AAV capsid, AAV.cc84, could deliver TREEs either pre- or post-cardiac injury to negate off-target expression in the liver while maintaining transduction in the heart.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing AAV9 and AAV.cc84 shown in Figure 2 and related experiments.

claim: AAV.IR41 is a new capsid variant with enhanced transduction in cardiac injuries and with elevated transduction of TREE-driven transgenes versus conventional AAV9 vectors.
source: By screening AAV9-based capsid libraries dosed systemically in mice post-cardiac injury, we discovered a new capsid variant, AAV.IR41, with enhanced transduction in cardiac injuries and with elevated transduction of TREE-driven transgenes versus conventional AAV9 vectors.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from capsid library screening and validation experiments shown in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: Many genes have been implicated by genetic studies in zebrafish and mouse to elevate or restrict cardiomyocyte (CM) proliferation after cardiac injury.
source: Many genes have been implicated by genetic studies in zebrafish and mouse to elevate or restrict cardiomyocyte (CM) proliferation after cardiac injury, with groups targeting factors controlling differentiation, chromatin state, metabolism, and other events (Eulalio et al., 2012; Choi et al., 2013; Fang et al., 2013; Mahmoud et al., 2013; Karra et al., 2015; Bassat et al., 2017; Toischer et al., 2017; Hirose et al., 2019; Chen et al., 2021; Li et al., 2023; Nguyen et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior published work.

claim: Notable mitogenic influences include the secreted factor Neuregulin1 (Nrg1), signaling through ErbB family receptors.
source: Notable mitogenic influences include the secreted factor Neuregulin1 (Nrg1), signaling through ErbB family receptors (Bersell et al., 2009; D'Uva et al., 2015; Gemberling et al., 2015)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: The transcription factor Klf1 is a notable mitogenic influence on cardiomyocyte proliferation.
source: Notable mitogenic influences include the secreted factor Neuregulin1 (Nrg1), signaling through ErbB family receptors (Bersell et al., 2009; D'Uva et al., 2015; Gemberling et al., 2015), the transcription factor (TF) Klf1 (Ogawa et al., 2021)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior published work.

claim: Yap/Taz factors are notable mitogenic influences that are normally restrained from the nucleus by Hippo in cardiomyocytes.
source: Notable mitogenic influences include the secreted factor Neuregulin1 (Nrg1), signaling through ErbB family receptors (Bersell et al., 2009; D'Uva et al., 2015; Gemberling et al., 2015), the transcription factor (TF) Klf1 (Ogawa et al., 2021), and Yap/Taz factors, normally restrained from the nucleus by Hippo in CMs (von Gise et al., 2012; Heallen et al., 2013; Xin et al., 2013; Morikawa et al., 2015; Bassat et al., 2017; Leach et al., 2017; Morikawa et al., 2017; Monroe et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior published work.

claim: The signaling environment for cardiomyocyte regeneration is complex, with epicardium, endocardium, nerves, macrophages, T cells, vasculature, and oxygen levels each influencing CM regeneration.
source: The signaling environment is complex, with epicardium, endocardium, nerves, macrophages, T cells, vasculature, and oxygen levels each influencing CM regeneration (Lepilina et al., 2006; Kim et al., 2010; Kikuchi et al., 2011; Aurora et al., 2014; Mahmoud et al., 2015; Wang et al., 2015; Hui et al., 2017; Nakada et al., 2017; Sugimoto et al., 2017; Zhao et al., 2019; Xia et al., 2022; Peterson et al., 2024; Shin et al., 2024; Sun et al., 2024; Weinberger et al., 2024).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior published work.

claim: TREEs were first described as distal regulatory elements that direct gene expression in regenerating zebrafish hearts.
source: Recently, distal regulatory elements referred to as tissue regeneration enhancer elements (TREEs) were described that direct gene expression in regenerating zebrafish hearts, a new concept for the field of regenerative biology (Kang et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the original work describing TREEs.

claim: TREEs have been identified by chromatin profiling in cardiomyocytes, epicardium, and other tissues of zebrafish like spinal cord and fins.
source: TREEs have been identified by chromatin profiling in CMs, epicardium, and other tissues of zebrafish like spinal cord and fins (Goldman et al., 2017; Thompson et al., 2020; Cao et al., 2022; Cigliola et al., 2023)
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior published work.

claim: TREEs have been identified in a variety of other species, tissues, and injury contexts beyond zebrafish.
source: TREEs have been identified by chromatin profiling in CMs, epicardium, and other tissues of zebrafish like spinal cord and fins (Goldman et al., 2017; Thompson et al., 2020; Cao et al., 2022; Cigliola et al., 2023), as well as in a variety of other species, tissues, and injury contexts (Harris et al., 2016; Vizcaya-Molina et al., 2018; Gehrke et al., 2019; Harris et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2020; Jimenez et al., 2022; Sun et al., 2022; Suzuki et al., 2022; Li et al., 2023; Sun and Poss, 2023; Zlatanova et al., 2023; Kawaguchi et al., 2024).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior published work.

claim: TREEs of zebrafish origin can be recognized by the transcriptional machinery of small mammals (mice) or even large mammals (pigs).
source: Critically, TREEs of zebrafish origin can be recognized by the transcriptional machinery of small (mice) or even large (pigs) mammals.
evidence: This claim is supported by prior published work and experimental data.

claim: Systemic introduction of AAV vectors with TREE-cargo cassettes can spatiotemporally target factor delivery to the injured mammalian heart or spinal cord.
source: Systemic introduction of adeno-associated viral (AAV) vectors with TREE-cargo cassettes can spatiotemporally target factor delivery to the injured mammalian heart or spinal cord (Cigliola et al., 2023; Yan et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: A TREE paired with a heavily mutated YAP transgene transiently directs expression to the border zone of a mouse heart injured by ischemia/reperfusion, stimulating localized cardiomyocyte cycling and functional recovery.
source: For instance, a TREE paired with a heavily mutated YAP transgene transiently directs expression to the border zone of a mouse heart injured by ischemia/reperfusion (I/R), stimulating localized CM cycling and functional recovery (Yan et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior published work.

claim: Short TREE sequences found in zebrafish can act as targeting vehicles for regenerative augmentation.
source: Thus, short TREE sequences found in zebrafish, and presumably elements with similar properties from other organisms, can act as targeting vehicles for regenerative augmentation.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental evidence and prior work cited in the manuscript.

claim: New engineered and variant forms of AAV capsids have been developed to modulate tissue tropism and cell type specificity.
source: Recently, new engineered and variant forms of AAV capsids have been developed to modulate tissue tropism and cell type specificity, such as liver de-targeting with AAV.cc84 (Gonzalez et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior published work.

claim: AAV.cc84 is a liver de-targeting capsid variant.
source: Recently, new engineered and variant forms of AAV capsids have been developed to modulate tissue tropism and cell type specificity, such as liver de-targeting with AAV.cc84 (Gonzalez et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior published work and experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: The strong, constitutively active CBA promoter directs robust fLuc expression across the mouse body.
source: As expected, the strong, constitutively active CBA promoter directed robust fLuc expression across the mouse body, whereas mice transduced with AAV9 harboring Hspa1a::fLuc had relatively minimal luminescence, mostly originating from the liver (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Mice transduced with AAV9 harboring Hspa1a::fLuc had relatively minimal luminescence, mostly originating from the liver.
source: As expected, the strong, constitutively active CBA promoter directed robust fLuc expression across the mouse body, whereas mice transduced with AAV9 harboring Hspa1a::fLuc had relatively minimal luminescence, mostly originating from the liver (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Luminescence in the heart, liver, and whole-body plateaued and remained stable from 30 to 68 days post-AAV delivery for both CBA and Hspa1a vectors.
source: Luminescence in the heart, liver, and whole-body plateaued and remained stable from 30 to 68 days post-AAV delivery for both CBA and Hspa1a vectors, as indicated by average radiance measurement (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–E.

claim: Transduction of either REN or 2ankrd1aEN TREE sequences resulted in a marked increase in bioluminescence signal in the thoracic cage overlying the heart after I/R injury.
source: Transduction of either TREE sequence resulted in a marked increase in bioluminescence signal in the thoracic cage overlying the heart.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and C.

claim: Bioluminescence from TREE-directed expression peaked within the first 3 days after I/R and returned to pre-injury baseline levels within 35 days post-injury.
source: Bioluminescence peaked within the first 3 days after I/R and returned to pre-injury baseline levels within 35 days post-injury (dpi) (Figure 1B and C; n=2 mice).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and C.

claim: Cardiac bioluminescence showed no change after sham surgery for all TREE-containing AAV vectors, indicating that TREE-directed expression occurred in response to myocardial trauma.
source: Cardiac bioluminescence showed no change after sham surgery for all mice, indicating that TREE-directed expression occurred in response to myocardial trauma (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Each AAV vector (CBA, Hspa1a, and TREE) demonstrated off-target expression in the abdominal region directly above the liver after transduction.
source: Notably, each AAV vector (CBA, Hspa1a, and TREE) demonstrated off-target expression in the abdominal region directly above the liver after transduction, which was also indicated to a limited degree by histology in our previous study (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B; Yan et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, as well as a citation to prior work.

claim: AAV.cc84 showed no detectable signal in the liver for all sexes of mice over 35 days following AAV delivery.
source: IVIS images revealed off-target luminescence in male and female livers with AAV9, whereas AAV.cc84 showed no detectable signal in the liver for all sexes of mice over 35 days following AAV (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: AAV9 enabled substantially higher expression in liver than AAV.cc84.
source: Quantification indicated that AAV9 enabled substantially higher expression in liver than AAV.cc84, which remained minimal over time (Figure 2C, n=6 mice).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Luminescence in the heart was similar between AAV9 and AAV.cc84.
source: Luminescence in the heart was similar between AAV9 and AAV.cc84, and, as expected, luminescence showed no change upon sham surgery (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: AAV9-injected mice contained a much higher viral load in liver tissue compared to AAV.cc84, for both males and females.
source: Vector genome quantification by qPCR revealed AAV9-injected mice contained a much higher viral load in liver tissue compared to AAV.cc84, for both males and females (Figure 2E, n=3 mice).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Vector genomes in the heart were similar between AAV9 and AAV.cc84 for both sexes of mice.
source: Vector genomes in the heart were similar between AAV9 and AAV.cc84 for both sexes of mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: AAV.cc84 can be implemented to minimize off-target liver expression of TREEs, evading liver transduction while maintaining cardiac tropism.
source: These results indicate that AAV.cc84 can be implemented to minimize off-target liver expression of TREEs, evading liver transduction while maintaining cardiac tropism.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data presented in Figure 2 and related experiments.

claim: 2ankrd1aEN-Hspa1a::fLuc-transduced mice showed robust fLuc activity in the thoracic cage overlying the heart, which increased up to 28 dpi and plateaued afterwards.
source: 2ankrd1aEN-Hspa1a::fLuc-transduced mice showed robust fLuc activity in the thoracic cage overlying the heart, which increased up to 28 dpi and plateaued afterwards (Figure 3B and C; n=4 mice).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B and C.

claim: Cardiac bioluminescence in Hspa1a::fLuc-transduced mice remained relatively minimal over time after I/R injury.
source: Conversely, cardiac bioluminescence in Hspa1a::fLuc-transduced mice remained relatively minimal over time (Figure 3B and C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B; n=4 mice).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B, C, and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: 2ankrd1aEN-directed cardiac expression was elevated approximately threefold in mice with I/R injury compared to sham at 7 dpi.
source: IVIS imaging revealed a baseline of 2ankrd1aEN-directed cardiac expression in sham-operated mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C), which was elevated approximately threefold in mice with I/R injury compared to sham at 7 dpi (Figure 3D, n=4 mice).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: 2ankrd1aEN-directed bioluminescence in the heart increased during the first 28 days for sham-operated mice, likely indicative of increased AAV transduction and transgene expression over time.
source: 2ankrd1aEN-directed bioluminescence in the heart increased during the first 28 days for sham-operated mice, likely indicative of increased AAV transduction and transgene expression over time (noting that AAV deliveries in Figure 1 experiments were 60 days prior to luminescence measurements; Figure 3E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E and includes speculation about the mechanism.

claim: I/R injured mice maintained higher cardiac activity throughout the 63-day time course, with the greatest differences at 7 and 21 dpi.
source: Notably, I/R injured mice maintained higher cardiac activity throughout the 63-day time course, with the greatest differences at 7 and 21 dpi (Figure 3E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: 2ankrd1aEN directs long-lasting gene expression in the injured mouse heart.
source: Together, these results indicate that 2ankrd1aEN-directed gene expression can be estimated longitudinally over long time periods, and in agreement with our previous histological analysis, 2ankrd1aEN directs long-lasting gene expression in the injured mouse heart.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data and agreement with prior histological analysis.

claim: Directed evolution of AAV libraries has been previously used to discover new capsids with improved functional properties.
source: Directed evolution of AAV libraries has been previously used to discover new capsids with improved functional properties, such as liver de-targeting (AAV.cc84), enhanced potency (AAV.cc47), and tropism for specific cell types (AAV.ark313, AAV.k20) (Gonzalez et al., 2022; Gonzalez et al., 2023; Nyberg et al., 2023; Nyberg et al., 2025; Rosales et al., 2025).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior published work.

claim: AAV9 is observed to preferentially transduce border zones of infarcted myocardium when delivered acutely (10 min to 3 dpi) after injury.
source: A previous report indicated that AAV9 is observed to preferentially transduce border zones of infarcted myocardium when delivered acutely (10 min to 3 dpi) after injury, which was speculated to be driven by a combination of increased capillary permeability, sialidase activity, and DNA damage after cardiac ischemia (Konkalmatt et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior published work.

claim: Preferential transduction of border zones by AAV9 was speculated to be driven by a combination of increased capillary permeability, sialidase activity, and DNA damage after cardiac ischemia.
source: A previous report indicated that AAV9 is observed to preferentially transduce border zones of infarcted myocardium when delivered acutely (10 min to 3 dpi) after injury, which was speculated to be driven by a combination of increased capillary permeability, sialidase activity, and DNA damage after cardiac ischemia (Konkalmatt et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior published work that includes speculation.

claim: Three unique capsids were enriched in the infarcted tissue over remote for both I/R mice, while being comparably expressed in both biopsies of the sham mouse.
source: We found three unique capsids that were enriched in the infarcted tissue over remote for both I/R mice, while being comparably expressed in both biopsies of the sham mouse (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: AAV.IR41 transduced I/R-injured hearts more effectively than AAV9 and the other two variant capsids (IR42, IR43) when packaged with a CBA::EGFP transgene.
source: Of the three variant capsids, we found the capsid with the highest number of reads in infarcted tissue (AAV.IR41) transduced I/R-injured hearts more effectively than AAV9 and the other two variant capsids (IR42, IR43) when packaged with a CBA::EGFP transgene (Figure 4C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: When systemically delivered at 9 dpi, IR41 transduced larger areas of myocardium surrounding areas of infarct compared to AAV9.
source: When systemically delivered at 9 dpi, IR41 transduced larger areas of myocardium surrounding areas of infarct compared to AAV9 (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: AAV9 and IR41 primarily transduced cardiomyocytes directly at the border zone with similar effectiveness.
source: Using F-actin staining to mark the border zone, AAV9 and IR41 primarily transduced CMs directly at the border zone with similar effectiveness (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: EGFP did not notably co-localize with vimentin staining of non-myocytes for either AAV9 or IR41, thus both capsids still primarily transduce cardiomyocytes.
source: EGFP did not notably co-localize with vimentin staining of non-myocytes for either AAV9 or IR41, thus both capsids still primarily transduce CM (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Sequence-based screening identified a capsid with enhanced transduction and expression in injured myocardium.
source: Thus, sequence-based screening identified a capsid with enhanced transduction and expression in injured myocardium.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data presented in Figure 4.

claim: IVIS imaging revealed higher expression levels in animals transduced with IR41 compared to AAV9, in both sham and MI groups.
source: IVIS imaging revealed higher expression levels in animals transduced with IR41 compared to AAV9, in both sham and MI groups (Figure 5A, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A; n=3 mice).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Higher hepatic expression was noted in both sham and infarcted mice with IR41 compared to AAV9.
source: We also noted higher hepatic expression in both sham and infarcted mice with IR41 compared to AAV9 (Figure 5A), although no new tissue transduction was introduced as detectable by biodistribution and reporter gene expression.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The average and maximum radiances recorded in IR41-transduced mouse hearts were significantly higher than AAV9 by 7 dpi and remained elevated at 21 dpi.
source: The average and maximum radiances recorded in IR41-transduced mouse hearts were significantly higher than AAV9 by 7 dpi and remained elevated at 21 dpi (Figure 5B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B and C.

claim: IR41 had roughly twice as high viral uptake than AAV9 in mice given cardiac injuries.
source: Vector genome quantification by qPCR showed that IR41 had roughly twice as high viral uptake than AAV9 in mice given cardiac injuries (Figure 5D, n=3 mice).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: IR41-transduced mice showed a trend toward higher cardiac viral genome loads than AAV9-transduced mice upon sham injury, indicating that IR41 might increase tropism in uninjured hearts.
source: Interestingly, IR41-transduced mice showed a trend toward higher cardiac viral genome loads than AAV9-transduced mice upon sham injury, indicating that IR41 might increase tropism in uninjured hearts, but its effects will be greatest when delivered to injured hearts (Figure 5D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D and includes speculation about the mechanism.

claim: Increased tropism of AAV.IR41 for injured myocardium, defined by enhanced uptake and higher transgene expression versus control AAV9, can be complemented by injury-responsive TREEs for targeting cargo delivery to sites of cardiac damage.
source: Together, our experiments indicate that increased tropism of AAV.IR41 for injured myocardium, defined by enhanced uptake and higher transgene expression versus control AAV9, can be complemented by injury-responsive TREEs for targeting cargo delivery to sites of cardiac damage.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data presented in Figure 5.

claim: IVIS imaging for assessing amplitude and specificity of TREE-directed transgene expression will aid future development of enhancer-based gene therapies relevant to cardiac regeneration and disease.
source: Our study indicates that IVIS imaging for assessing amplitude and specificity of TREE-directed transgene expression will aid future development of enhancer-based gene therapies relevant to cardiac regeneration and disease.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data and represents a conclusion about future applications.

claim: With an IVIS imaging modality, effects of capsid alterations and enhancer sequence alterations can be efficiently and noninvasively assessed to refine their ability to target gene expression in the injured heart.
source: With an IVIS imaging modality, effects of capsid alterations and enhancer sequence alterations can be efficiently and noninvasively assessed to refine their ability to target gene expression in the injured heart.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data and represents a conclusion about the utility of the technique.

claim: Expression by internal organs must be approximated with potentially subjective ROIs that cannot be verified until harvesting the organs at sacrifice.
source: Expression by internal organs must also be approximated with potentially subjective ROIs that cannot be verified until harvesting the organs at sacrifice.
evidence: This is a limitation of the IVIS imaging technique acknowledged by the authors.

claim: Unexpected off-target TREE expression was observed in the liver, neck, and abdomen, which was modulated by capsid engineering.
source: Although the expression is approximated, we were able to observe unexpected off-target TREE expression in the liver, neck, and abdomen, which was modulated by capsid engineering.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the IVIS imaging experiments.

claim: Future work exploring cell surface markers or receptors is needed to better understand the apparent enhanced tropism of IR41 over AAV9.
source: Additionally, future work exploring cell surface markers or receptors is needed to better understand the apparent enhanced tropism of IR41 over AAV9, and to engineer liver detargeting attributes into this form.
evidence: This is a statement about future research directions based on the current findings.

claim: It is possible that combining the modifications in AAV.cc84 and AAV.IR41 would produce additive effects.
source: For instance, it is possible that combining the modifications in AAV.cc84 and AAV.IR41 would produce additive effects.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential future experiments.

claim: Larger animal models are not suited for IVIS imaging due to limitations of tissue penetrance.
source: Finally, larger animal models are not suited for IVIS imaging due to limitations of tissue penetrance, and findings in mice may not fully recapitulate those in larger animal models and humans.
evidence: This is a limitation of the IVIS imaging technique based on established knowledge.

claim: Findings in mice may not fully recapitulate those in larger animal models and humans.
source: Finally, larger animal models are not suited for IVIS imaging due to limitations of tissue penetrance, and findings in mice may not fully recapitulate those in larger animal models and humans.
evidence: This is a general limitation of mouse models based on established knowledge.

claim: The AAV capsid library screening was limited to mice, and capsid hits remain to be tested in other species.
source: Our AAV capsid library screening was limited to mice, and capsid hits remain to be tested in other species.
evidence: This is a limitation of the current study acknowledged by the authors.

claim: This work lays a foundation for refining TREE-targeted factor delivery to injured myocardium and expanding their use in applications for therapeutic tissue repair.
source: While further optimization is required, this work lays a foundation for refining TREE-targeted factor delivery to injured myocardium and expanding their use in applications for therapeutic tissue repair.
evidence: This is a concluding statement about the significance of the work based on the experimental findings.

claim: The procedure for I/R myocardial injury via temporary LCA ligation was adapted from previously described protocols.
source: The procedure for I/R myocardial injury via temporary LCA ligation was adapted from previously described protocols (Kaiser et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior published work.

claim: Occlusion of the LAD was confirmed by the anterior wall of the left ventricle turning a pale color.
source: Occlusion of the LAD was confirmed by the anterior wall of the left ventricle turning a pale color.
evidence: This is a methodological detail based on established knowledge of cardiac physiology.

claim: LAD occlusion was maintained for 40 min during I/R surgery.
source: LAD occlusion was maintained for 40 min.
evidence: This is a methodological detail from the experimental protocol.

claim: Reperfusion of the LAD was confirmed by the return of a pink-red color to the anterior wall.
source: After the ischemia period, the suture was untied, and reperfusion of the LAD was confirmed by the return of a pink-red color to the anterior wall.
evidence: This is a methodological detail based on established knowledge of cardiac physiology.

claim: AAV9-based capsid libraries were constructed using saturation mutagenesis of residues within the VR-IV site.
source: AAV9-based capsid libraries were constructed using saturation mutagenesis of residues within the VR-IV site as previously described (Gonzalez et al., 2023; Rosales et al., 2025).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: The VR-IV region of Cap was replaced with a partial GFP sequence to prevent incorporation of wild-type VR-IV sequences in the parental library.
source: Prior to saturation mutagenesis with degenerate primers, the VR-IV region of Cap was replaced with a partial GFP sequence to prevent incorporation of wild-type VR-IV sequences in the parental library.
evidence: This is a methodological detail from the experimental protocol.

claim: D-luciferin was injected intraperitoneally at 150 mg/kg b.w. dose for IVIS imaging.
source: While mice were anesthetized under 2% isoflurane, thawed D-luciferin was injected intraperitoneally at 150 mg/kg b.w. dose.
evidence: This is a methodological detail from the experimental protocol.

claim: Body hair above regions of interest was removed using Nair to improve signal-to-noise ratio in IVIS imaging.
source: Regions of interest for this study, such as the heart and liver, had body hair above them removed using Nair to improve signal-to-noise ratio.
evidence: This is a methodological detail from the experimental protocol.

claim: Luciferase signals were allowed a 10–15 min plateau time before imaging.
source: Luciferase signals were allowed a 10–15 min plateau time.
evidence: This is a methodological detail from the experimental protocol.

claim: The REN TREE was selected for liver de-targeting experiments because liver luminescence was more prominent with respect to the cardiac signal.
source: REN was selected as the liver luminescence was more prominent with respect to the cardiac signal in the above experiments.
evidence: This is a methodological decision based on experimental observations.

claim: Capsid libraries were delivered to mice at 9 dpi to limit the effects of acute changes after cardiac ischemia.
source: We attempted to limit the effects of these acute changes by delivering capsid libraries to mice that had undergone sham or I/R surgery at 9 dpi, when the acute inflammation phase is complete and the repair phase with myofibroblast activation and proliferation has begun (Figure 4A, n=2 mice).
evidence: This is a methodological decision based on knowledge of cardiac injury phases.

claim: At 9 dpi, the acute inflammation phase is complete and the repair phase with myofibroblast activation and proliferation has begun.
source: We attempted to limit the effects of these acute changes by delivering capsid libraries to mice that had undergone sham or I/R surgery at 9 dpi, when the acute inflammation phase is complete and the repair phase with myofibroblast activation and proliferation has begun (Figure 4A, n=2 mice).
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge of cardiac injury phases.

claim: IR41 has the VR4 peptide sequence GPGVGAR.
source: IR41 VR4 peptide sequence: GPGVGAR
evidence: This is a factual statement from the Key Resources Table.

claim: IR42 has the VR4 peptide sequence ASRNVVT.
source: IR42 VR4 peptide sequence: ASRNVVT
evidence: This is a factual statement from the Key Resources Table.

claim: IR43 has the VR4 peptide sequence SDSQYVQ.
source: IR43 VR4 peptide sequence: SDSQYVQ
evidence: This is a factual statement from the Key Resources Table.

claim: All mouse protocols were approved by the Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC) at Duke University.
source: All mouse protocols were approved by the Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC) at Duke University (Protocols #A003-22-01, #A025-24-01), which is accredited by the Association for Assessment and Accreditation of Laboratory Animal Care-International (AAALAC).
evidence: This is a statement about regulatory compliance.

claim: Wild-type male and female C57BL/6J and BALB/c mice were used for this study.
source: Wild-type male and female C57BL/6J (The Jackson Laboratory, Strain #000664) and BALB/c (Charles River, Strain #028) mice were used for this study.
evidence: This is a methodological detail about the animal models used.

claim: I/R procedures were performed in the Duke Cardiovascular Physiology Core.
